_comment: Every rule the engine can emit, with the source that justifies it. A test fails if the engine emits a ruleId absent from this file, so a rule cannot be added without saying where it comes from.

_tiers.normative: van Steenbergen’s grammar pages. The only tier that may be cited as authority for a claim about Interslavic.
_tiers.corpus: Attested usage, where the grammar pages are silent. Needed because there is no page on case usage at all.
_tiers.dictionary: A fact about one specific word from the dictionary, not a rule about the language.
_tiers.transfer: Copying something the SOURCE language states. Not a claim about Interslavic.
_tiers.structural: A mechanical consequence of the parse or of an earlier decision. Asserts nothing about Interslavic that needs a citation.

_quoteGap: Entries with quote: null are justified by the cited page but not yet pinned to a single verbatim sentence - usually because the page expresses the rule as a declension table. The test holds this count so it can only shrink.

agreement.fromHead.why: a modifier agrees with its head in gender, number and case - expressed by the declension tables rather than by a single sentence

agreement.impersonal.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
agreement.impersonal.why: an impersonal predicate is neuter singular, as the corpus writes it ("Nužno jest tuty članok prěvesti")

agreement.pastParticiple.quote: Most commonly used is the compound past, made by combining the present tense of the verb byti „to be” with the so-called L-participle.
agreement.pastParticiple.why: the l-participle is a participle, so it agrees with the subject in gender and number

agreement.predicate.why: a predicate adjective agrees with its subject and takes the nominative

agreement.predicate.defaultGender.why: a predicate adjective must have a gender and some subjects carry none; the unmarked masculine, reported as a default rather than a certainty

agreement.predicate.person.quote: Except for adjectives referring to masculine, animate nouns, the nominate and accusative plural are identical for all genders.
agreement.predicate.person.why: a 1st/2nd person subject is a person, so the predicate is animate

agreement.relative.quote: Relative pronouns (Odnositeljne zaimenniky) The relative pronoun that is used most frequently is ktory.
agreement.relative.why: the relative pronoun ktory agrees with its antecedent

anaphora.one.why: English-side analysis: placeholder "one" is not a word to translate, and the adjective left behind agrees with the antecedent instead

animacy.lexical.quote: In the case of animate nouns (animals and male persons) the accusative is always identical to the genitive, while in the case of inanimate nouns it is identical to the nominative.
animacy.lexical.why: animacy decides the accusative, and the dictionary states it per noun

animacy.noAnimateHead.quote: In the case of animate nouns (animals and male persons) the accusative is always identical to the genitive, while in the case of inanimate nouns it is identical to the nominative.
animacy.noAnimateHead.why: the accusative of an inanimate equals its nominative

aspect.adverbial.imp.quote: Imperfective aspect, on the other hand, focuses on action itself; it indicates that on the point of reference the action is or was going on. It can also express a an ongoing process, a habit or a repeated action
aspect.adverbial.imp.why: a habitual or iterative adverbial forces the imperfective

aspect.adverbial.perf.quote: Using the present tense of a perfective verb for the future (as is done in West and East Slavic) is rather to be avoided, as it can easily be misunderstood by South Slavs.
aspect.adverbial.perf.why: an adverbial naming a single completed event forces the perfective; the aspect pair is the distinction this quote turns on

aspect.default.imp.quote: Using the present tense of a perfective verb for the future (as is done in West and East Slavic) is rather to be avoided, as it can easily be misunderstood by South Slavs.
aspect.default.imp.why: the imperfective is the safe default for the same reason

aspect.lexemeOverride.why: the aspect the chosen lexeme actually has, which outranks an inferred one

aspect.pastGoal.quote: In short, perfective aspect focuses on the result of an action and not on the action itself. Depending on tense, it means that the action has been completed already or will be completed at some point.
aspect.pastGoal.why: a past movement to a goal reached it, so it is a completed event with a result; only a goal bounds it, so durative and habitual movements stay imperfective

aspect.pastTelic.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
aspect.pastTelic.why: a completed past event takes the perfective; the grammar states the distinction but gives no mechanical test, so the choice follows attested usage

aspect.perfect.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
aspect.perfect.why: an English perfect describes a completed event, so the perfective

aspect.tense.presImp.quote: Using the present tense of a perfective verb for the future (as is done in West and East Slavic) is rather to be avoided, as it can easily be misunderstood by South Slavs.
aspect.tense.presImp.why: a present tense takes the imperfective, because a perfective present reads as a future

aspect.tense.progressive.quote: Using the present tense of a perfective verb for the future (as is done in West and East Slavic) is rather to be avoided, as it can easily be misunderstood by South Slavs.
aspect.tense.progressive.why: an English progressive describes an action in progress, so the imperfective - and a perfective present would read as a future

case.coordination.why: a conjunct copies its head’s case; a preposition governs the whole coordination, not just its first member

case.copy.why: Russian marks case explicitly, so it is copied rather than inferred

case.deprel.iobj.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
case.deprel.iobj.why: an indirect object takes the dative

case.deprel.nsubj.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
case.deprel.nsubj.why: a subject takes the nominative. The grammar has NO page on case usage - cases.html, case.html and accusative.html all 404 - which is why this tier exists

case.deprel.obj.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
case.deprel.obj.why: a direct object takes the accusative, absent a government code

case.durationAccusative.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
case.durationAccusative.why: a bare duration takes the accusative

case.fallback.why: the honest last resort when no rule applies; emitted at `guess` confidence so it is visible as such

case.fromCountingNumeral.quote: The subject always remains in the genitive plural.
case.fromCountingNumeral.why: and it persists in oblique positions

case.phrasalObject.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
case.phrasalObject.why: a complement whose English preposition was absorbed by a phrasal verb becomes that verb’s direct object, so the accusative unless the verb has its own government code

case.predicate.why: a predicate complement takes the nominative

case.prep.governed.quote: Prepositions should only be used according to their logical meaning, not according to national idioms.
case.prep.governed.why: each preposition governs a stated case; the table on this page is the source

case.temporalAccusative.source: corpus: van Steenbergen’s parallel texts and the Interslavic Wikipedia (incubator.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wp/isv)
case.temporalAccusative.why: a bare time adverbial takes the accusative

case.verbGovernedPrep.why: the preposition a verb governs lexically

copula.inserted.why: Interslavic writes the present copula where Russian omits it

degree.comparative.quote: Comparatives and superlatives can be built in two ways: a simple (analytic) form and a more complex (synthetic) form.

degree.superlative.quote: The superlative is formed by adding the prefix naj- to the comparative: najnovějši

future.agreement.quote: The future tense is formed by combining the future tense of the verb byti „to be” with the infinitive.
future.agreement.why: the budu auxiliary carries the person and number

future.periphrastic.quote: The future tense is formed by combining the future tense of the verb byti „to be” with the infinitive.
future.periphrastic.why: budu plus the infinitive, not a conjugated verb

gender.lexical.why: the noun’s gender, from its partOfSpeech cell

gender.pronounLemma.why: the gender of the chosen Interslavic pronoun lemma

mood.conditional.quote: The conditional is be formed by using the L-participle with the conditional of byti „to be”: ja byh dělal(a) „I would do”.

mood.imperative.quote: The imperative has forms for the 2nd person singular, the 1st person plural and the 2nd person plural: dělaj „do!” (to one person, informal), dělajmo „let’s do!”, dělajte „do!” (to more persons, or to one person formal).

mood.indicative.quote: There are three moods: indicative, conditional and imperative.
mood.indicative.why: the unmarked mood of the three the language has

negation.beforeVerb.quote: Negation in Interslavic can always be recognized by the particle ne „not” preceding the verb.
negation.beforeVerb.why: ne precedes the verb it negates

number.fromSubject.why: a verb’s number comes from its SUBJECT, not from its own features or its auxiliary - a plural nominal subject often leaves the English verb unmarked

number.pluraleTantum.why: nouns the dictionary marks pl. only

number.pronounLemma.why: the number of the chosen Interslavic pronoun, which is a property of that lemma: English "you" is unmarked but `vy` is plural

number.singulareTantum.why: nouns the dictionary marks sg. only

numeral.government.quote: All numbers higher than 4 are followed by the genitive plural: pet domov
numeral.government.why: 5 and up govern the genitive plural

optative.nehaj.quote: nehaj is used: Nehaj umre! „Let him die!” Nehaj žive dolgo! „May he live long!”
optative.nehaj.why: a third-person command uses nehaj plus the present

optative.present.quote: nehaj is used: Nehaj umre! „Let him die!” Nehaj žive dolgo! „May he live long!”
optative.present.why: the verb after nehaj stays in the present

passive.participle.quote: Koja žena jest ljubjena od togo muža? „Which woman is loved by that man?”
passive.participle.why: a participial passive with od plus the genitive for the agent

past.compoundAuxiliary.quote: Most commonly used is the compound past, made by combining the present tense of the verb byti „to be” with the so-called L-participle.
past.compoundAuxiliary.why: the byti auxiliary the compound past needs beside its l-participle

past.lParticiple.quote: Most commonly used is the compound past, made by combining the present tense of the verb byti „to be” with the so-called L-participle.
past.lParticiple.why: a past tense is the l-participle plus the present of byti

person.fromSubject.why: a verb’s person comes from its SUBJECT; English auxiliaries mislead, and Stanza tags "did" as Person=2

pronoun.prepCase.quote: After a preposition, it is better to use the longer forms: k mně, za tebe.
pronoun.prepCase.why: the long pronoun form after a preposition

purpose.conditional.quote: Ona prinosi jabloka, da by děti byli zdrave.
purpose.conditional.why: a purpose clause is da by plus the l-participle

reflexive.clitic.quote: Even more common is a reflexive construction: Pica dělaje se, which literally means „Pizza is making itself” and should be translated as „One makes pizza, pizza is being made”.
reflexive.clitic.why: the clitic is written as a separate word

rewrite.en.'sAsCase.why: English-side analysis: the possessive clitic is a case, not a word, so it is not translated

rewrite.en.ofAsCase.why: English-side analysis: "of" marks the genitive rather than being a preposition to translate

rewrite.en.toAsCase.why: English-side analysis: "to" before a recipient marks the dative

tense.perfectAsPast.why: an English perfect maps onto the Interslavic past; there is no separate perfect

verbform.finite.why: a finite clause takes a conjugated verb

verbform.modalComplement.why: the complement of a modal is an infinitive, so it must not be conjugated

gender.fromEnding.quote: The first declension includes all masculine nouns ending in a consonant, as well as neuter nouns ending in -o or -e . The second declension includes all feminine nouns on -a .
gender.fromEnding.why: a name the dictionary does not have is declined by its ending: a consonant is masculine, -a feminine, -o/-e neuter

animacy.unknownName.quote: In the case of animate nouns (animals and male persons) the accusative is always identical to the genitive, while in the case of inanimate objects the accusative is identical to the nominative.
animacy.unknownName.why: animacy decides only the accusative, and the parse does not say whether an unknown name is a person, so the inanimate (nominative-like) accusative is kept as a visible guess

verbform.transgressive.quote: The adverbial present active participle (also known as „transgressive”) has the same ending, but is not inflected for gender: Iduči do raboty, ona vsegda dymi cigaretoju „While going to her work, she always smokes a cigarette”.
verbform.transgressive.why: an English -ing clause with no subject of its own, simultaneous with the main verb, is the adverbial present participle, which is not inflected
